solved.q: Using elementary row transformation R2 -> R2 - 2R1, transform A = [[1, 2],[2, 5]].
Find the inverse of A = [[3, 1],[5, 2]] using the adjoint method.
steps: Since det A is not zero, A inverse exists.
Cofactor matrix: [[2, -5],[-1, 3]]. Adjoint = transpose of cofactor matrix = [[2, -1],[-5, 3]].

solved.q: Find the inverse of A = [[1, 1, 1],[1, -1, 1],[2, 1, -1]] by the adjoint method.
steps: Since det A = 6 is not zero, A inverse exists.
Compute all 9 cofactors using 2x2 minors with sign (-1)^(i+j); cofactor matrix comes out to [[0, 3, 3],[2, -3, 1],[2, 0, -2]].

solved.q: Find the inverse of A = [[2, 1],[1, 1]] using elementary row transformations.
steps: Apply R1 <-> R2 to get a leading 1: [[1, 1 | 0, 1],[2, 1 | 1, 0]].
Left block is now I, so the right block is A inverse.

solved.topic: Solving linear equations by matrix inverse method
solved.q: Solve the following system using the matrix inverse method: x + y + z = 6, x - y + z = 2, 2x + y - z = 1.
steps: det A = 6 (computed as in the adjoint example above), so A inverse exists.
Verify: 1+2+3=6, 1-2+3=2, 2(1)+2-3=1 - all three equations are satisfied.

solved.q: Solve by the reduction method: x + 2y - z = 3, 2x - y + z = 4, 4x + 3y - 2z = 10.
If A = [[1, 2],[2, 3]], verify that (A inverse) inverse = A.
steps: Now find inverse of A inverse: det(A inverse) = (-3)(-1) - (2)(2) = 3 - 4 = -1.
This equals the original matrix A.

solved.topic: Inverse of a product (AB)^-1 = B^-1 A^-1
solved.q: If A = [[1, 0],[0, 2]] and B = [[1, 1],[0, 1]], verify (AB) inverse = B inverse * A inverse.
steps: A inverse = [[1, 0],[0, 1/2]] (since A is diagonal, invert each diagonal entry).
B inverse: det B = 1, adj B = [[1, -1],[0, 1]], so B inverse = [[1, -1],[0, 1]].
solved.ans: (AB) inverse = B inverse * A inverse = [[1, -1/2],[0, 1/2]], verified.

solved.topic: Elementary transformation to find rank-type reduction
solved.q: Reduce A = [[1, 2, 3],[2, 4, 7]] to row echelon form using elementary row transformation.
Find k if A = [[k, 2],[3, 4]] is a singular matrix (i.e. A inverse does not exist).
steps: A matrix is singular when its determinant is zero.
